fields.name: edit_mask_mode
fields.label: Region Mode
fields.tooltip: How the region mask is honored: auto (DiffSynth ControlNet if its weights are present, else crop+stitch), crop_stitch (crop to the mask + context, edit the crop, composite back — pixels outside the mask never change), full_frame (legacy whole-image edit; unmasked regions may drift).

fields.name: edit_context_pad
fields.label: Context Padding
fields.tooltip: Pixels of surrounding context kept in the crop (crop_stitch mode). More context = more coherent edit; 64 is the sweet spot.

fields.name: mask_grow
fields.label: Grow / Shrink
fields.tooltip: Expand (+) or shrink (−) the edit region by an exact pixel disk before the edit. Applied host-side — the same mask-prep chain the Inpaint card uses.

fields.name: mask_feather
fields.label: Feather
fields.tooltip: Gaussian falloff the composite blends through — kills the pasted-on rectangle edge.

fields.name: mask_threshold
fields.label: Re-threshold
fields.tooltip: Re-binarize the feathered mask at this level. 0 = keep the soft falloff.

fields.name: mask_invert
fields.label: Invert
fields.tooltip: Edit OUTSIDE the painted region instead.

variants.label: ⚡ Lightning (4-step)
variants.hint: The 4-step distilled checkpoint — official 2511 with lightx2v's Lightning distillation FUSED into FP8 weights (not stacked on top). One weights slot, one artifact, one route.

variants.label: Standard (20-step)
variants.hint: Reference workflow: 20 steps, cfg 2.5. Highest quality path — the INT8 ConvRot merge.

variants.label: INT8 ConvRot
variants.hint: ApexArtist community merge (NOT official Qwen): Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 + a lightx2v Lightning distillation + Next Scene + Multi-Angles LoRAs, INT8 ConvRot quantized. Which Lightning checkpoint (4- vs 8-step) the merge baked in is NOT stated upstream; the catalog runs it 8 steps / cfg 1.0 (bc59d544). Stacking the external 4-step LoRA on weights that already carry a distillation is double-distillation — the ⚡ row is not offered on this route.

Variant.label: Variant
Variant.tooltip: Step count / speed character. Each variant exists ONLY where its weights exist: ⚡ Lightning is the lightx2v FUSED FP8 checkpoint (its one artifact, its one route); Standard is the 20-step pass on the INT8 ConvRot merge. The loader auto-scopes each row to the routes its own cells declare — a variant × quant pairing with no artifact behind it can never be offered here.

Quant.label: Quant
Quant.tooltip: Quantization tier — INT8 ConvRot (the ApexArtist merge: official 2511 + a baked Lightning distillation + Next Scene + Multi-Angles LoRAs) on the Standard row / FP8 Lightning (official 2511 with lightx2v's 4-step distillation FUSED into the fp8 weights — the one honest 4-step route: single distillation, nothing stacked) on the ⚡ row. The Q8/Q5 GGUF tiers were retired 2026-08-21 — ComfyUI-approved safetensors only. All run through ComfyUI workflows.

fields.name: artifact
fields.label: Artifact
fields.tooltip: Flow-wired Conditioning source — the ctx artifact name (e.g. ``back_pose``) produced by an upstream brick. Takes precedence over image_b64 at run time: when the artifact is present in ctx, the brick uploads THAT file as the Conditioning image. Set by the flow YAML (``controlnets: [{type: openpose, artifact: back_pose, ...}]``) and surfaced read-only in the card so the user can see which upstream brick feeds this CN.

options.label: Region Inpaint (DiffSynth)
options.tooltip: Lock edits to a selection. Best with rectangular selections — the underlying training data is rectangular redraw, so soft / irregular masks may produce visible boundary artifacts. When this ControlNet is missing, "Edit with Qwen…" falls back to rectangle crop+edit+paste.

modifiers.label: Image Ops

fields.name: target_size
fields.label: Target Size
fields.tooltip: Output resolution. The advance node only accepts these six values; a free-form number would crash ComfyUI with prompt_outputs_failed_validation.

fields.name: vl_encoder_size
fields.label: VL Encoder Size
fields.tooltip: Resolution the vision-language encoder sees. Lower is faster but weaker prompt adherence; higher sharpens text/region following.

fields.name: crop_method
fields.label: Crop Method
fields.tooltip: How to fit a non-square input into the target box. "pad" letterboxes; "center" center-crops; "disabled" passes the image through unchanged (aspect ratio must already match).

modifiers.tooltip: Optional image-resize controls (target resolution, VL encoder size, resampler, crop). Absent from the run until you add this subcard; when absent, the model defaults (target_size, resample_method, …) apply unchanged.

sections.label: Strength
sections.body: Excellent at text rendering in images and instruction-based editing.

sections.label: Text in images
list_: Wrap text in double quotes: `poster reading "SALE 50% OFF"`
Chinese text rendering is especially strong
For signs/posters — describe content, font style, and layout

sections.label: What to use in ComfyUI
sections.body: The DiffSynth blockwise ControlNet (Region Inpaint subcard) is the only Qwen-Image-Edit ControlNet this stack can load — it locks edits to a selection. Pose/depth/canny controlnets are NOT available on edit_image: the 2512 Fun Union file (Qwen-Image-2512-Fun-Controlnet-Union-2602.safetensors) is a VideoX-Fun diffusers format no ComfyUI loader understands (declarations removed 2026-08-14 — any such request fails loud at validation). Route pose through generate_image (z-image + openpose CN) instead — the character_cards / filmmaking pattern.

enhance_prompt:
You are a Qwen Image Edit prompting expert. The user wants to edit an existing image.

- This is an INSTRUCTION-BASED EDITING model — describe the CHANGE, not the final scene
- Start with an action verb: add, remove, replace, change, rotate, recolor, relight
- Be specific about WHAT should change
- Explicitly state what should STAY THE SAME
- For multi-image edits, label each: 'Picture 1: a man. Picture 2: a hat. Put the hat from picture 2 on the man from picture 1.'
- Qwen Image Edit renders text well — wrap text in double quotes for replacements
- Keep the edit instruction concise — 20-80 words
- Do NOT describe the entire resulting image — just the modification

Write the prompt as continuous descriptive prose — NOT comma-separated tag lists. Natural language produces better results than keyword stacks on these models.

## Structure (order matters — lead with what's most important)
1. Subject identity and core action/pose
2. Detailed physical description — body, face, hair, clothing, textures
3. Hand/object interactions and spatial details
4. Background/environment with depth layers — near, mid, far
5. Lighting, atmosphere, and color palette
6. Camera/lens/framing (only if photorealistic)

## Enhancement Methodology
1. Lock the user's core intent — subject, action, colors, text are IMMUTABLE
2. If the request is abstract, construct a complete visualizable scene first
3. Inject professional aesthetics: composition, lighting, material textures, color scheme, spatial depth
4. Any text that should appear IN the image must be in double quotes: sign reading "OPEN"
5. Output must be objective and concrete. No metaphors or emotional rhetoric

## What to include
- Specific demographics when relevant: "young Chinese woman" not "woman"
- Facial features, expression, gaze direction
- Hair: style, color, length, accessories
- Garments named specifically: "cream-colored wool turtleneck" not "sweater"
- Fabric behavior: "slightly wrinkled linen", "glossy patent leather"
- Spatial positions: "on the left", "in the foreground", "behind her"
- Light source, direction, color temperature: "warm golden-hour sunlight from camera left"
- Camera details for photorealism: "85mm portrait lens, shallow depth of field"

## What NEVER to include
- Meta-tags: "8K", "masterpiece", "best quality", "highly detailed", "trending on artstation"
- Other-model syntax: "score_9", "plms", "euler a", "dpm++ 2m"
- Negation in positive prompts: "no hat" → rephrase as "bareheaded"
- Empty/vague backgrounds — always describe the environment

Chinese and English both work natively — you may mix them.

## Output format — STRICT
Return ONLY a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no explanation, no
text before or after. The whole response must be parseable by JSON.parse.

Schema:
  {"positive": "<the enhanced positive prompt>", "negative": "<negative prompt or empty string>"}

Rules:
- "positive" is always filled with the enhanced prompt per the methodology above.
- "negative" is filled with an effective negative prompt IF the model uses
  negatives (you noted whether it does above). Otherwise set "negative" to "".
- Both values are plain strings. Escape inner quotes and newlines per JSON.
- Never wrap the whole response in extra quotes. The JSON object itself is
  the response.
